subject: QuantumAI demo — follow-up & proposed bakeoff test plan
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@quantumai.com>, Ryan Shaw <ryan@quantumai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: QuantumAI demo — follow-up & proposed bakeoff test plan

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the candid discussion and the sample prompts you shared. This note recaps our understanding and proposes a lightweight bakeoff so you can directly compare Redwood against your current hyperscaler endpoints. Quick summary from the call: 

- Main goals: reduce per-token cost while keeping hallucination/factuality in check for QAI's Research Notes ingestion pipeline; maintain 75ms median latency target for summary requests.
- Primary constraints: some prompts contain long context windows (~6k tokens) and require stable KV-cache behavior; data residency (US) is required for PII data.
- Decision criteria (what QAI cares about): factuality/hallucination rate on entity extraction and summaries, 95th percentile latency, per-1k-token unit cost, and rollout simplicity (A/B/canary).

Proposed 2-week bakeoff (high level) — items we can run in parallel: 
1) Quality sweep: run QAI's priority prompts (attached: qai-priority-prompts.txt) against three endpoints: Redwood-hosted (recommended config), GCP Vertex, and AWS Bedrock. Metric targets: hallucination < 2% on entity extraction (see Karthik's note for definition), summary Factuality > 0.92, and no regression on your existing golden set.
2) Latency/Throughput: 1k request synthetic run with median/P95 latency, with both streaming and non-streaming configurations. Target median < 75ms for short prompts, P95 < 450ms.
3) Cost estimation: run token-consumption analysis on the same prompt set and produce per-100k-token cost estimates (we'll include quantized variants).
4) Reliability/rollout: canary plan and fallback behavior for model variants; smoke tests for KV-cache correctness on long-context prompts.

Owners & next steps I propose: 
- Redwood: Laura (AE) will coordinate scheduling and access, Marissa (Product) will run the bakeoff matrix and deliver results, Karthik (Applied ML) will own quality metric definitions and regression checks.
- QuantumAI: Eva to share prioritized prompt set + a short golden set (50 examples) and identify one procurement contact for timelines.

Timeline: start the week of Jun 17 (can start earlier for the quality sweep), deliver preliminary results within 10 business days.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-testplan.csv (test matrix stub), demo-recording.mp4 (demo).

Next call: propose Tues Jun 18 at 10am PT to walk the test plan and the HubSpot deal playbook. If that doesn't work share a few slots.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett

Laura — thanks for the thorough recap and for spelling out the decision criteria. We like the proposed structure and are happy to proceed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt set: attaching a prioritized list (qai-priority-prompts.txt). Top 3 buckets: Research notes summarization, entity extraction for citations, and creative rewrite prompts for marketing.
2) Hallucination metric: we define a hallucination as any generated entity/claim that is not verifiable in the source context or the provided knowledge base. For entity extraction we prefer precision-focused thresholds (we'd rather miss an entity than hallucinate one). Can you confirm Redwood's exact definition and how you'll compute the < 2% number?
3) Security/procurement: Ryan will loop in procurement if we move past the bakeoff. Can you confirm Redwood's SOC2 status and whether you have a quick checklist we can share internally?

Attached: qai-priority-prompts.txt (50 prioritized prompts). Demo follow-up: the team liked how the streaming preview felt — curious if stitching across segments will be part of the KV/cache checks.

Thanks,

Looping in a slightly more concrete test matrix and owners so we can get going. I put together a quick CSV (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.csv) that enumerates the runs we recommend. High level notes: 

- Quality matrix (owner: Karthik): golden set evaluation, entity-extraction precision/recall, factuality score distribution, and hallucination spot checks (manual sampling + automated checks).
- Latency/throughput (owner: Naomi): synthetic client with increasing concurrency (1/8/32) and both streaming enabled/disabled. We'll record median/P95/P99 and token throughput.
- Cost runs (owner: Marissa): run identical prompt set across model variants (float vs quantized) and produce normalized per-100k-token costs.
- Hyperscaler comparison: we'll run against Vertex + Bedrock + Azure OpenAI (if you have a preferred vendor we can add). Please confirm any endpoints you'd like included.

Acceptance criteria proposal (so we have alignment): 
- Hallucination threshold: <= 2% false-positive entity insertions on the priority prompts (manual adjudication on a 200-sample set).
- Summary factuality: mean Factuality Score >= 0.92 (automated metric + spot checks).
- Latency: median < 75ms for short prompts, P95 < 450ms.

I've attached the CSV matrix and a short runbook. If this looks good I'll schedule the runs and share an internal tracking doc (Drive link).

Best,

Adding technical definitions and the regression checklist so expectations are clear. Short version below (I'll drop a g-doc with exact scripts).

Hallucination definition (entity extraction): an extracted entity is a hallucination if it cannot be matched to any substring of the provided context or the canonical KB entries for that document. We'll run an automated matcher (case-insensitive, fuzzy threshold 0.85) and flag candidates for manual adjudication. The 2% target refers to false-positive rate after automated filtering and adjudication.

Quality metrics we'll compute: 
- Entity precision/recall (P/R), F1 for extraction tasks.
- Factuality Score for summaries (0-1) using a mix of entailment models + QA-based verification.
- Hallucination Rate (HR): # hallucinated tokens / # total generated tokens on the evaluation set (and an entity-level HR).

Regression checks (run on each commit of the evaluation harness): 
- Golden-set exact-match: >= baseline (no drop).
- Distributional checks: mean Factuality +/- 0.02 tolerated, tail regressions flagged.
- Behavioral probes: 30 targeted prompts that historically surface hallucinations (we'll add these to P0 test set).

Acceptance thresholds (initial, can be tightened with you): 
- Entity precision >= 0.98 on the golden set.
- Factuality mean >= 0.92.
- Hallucination Rate (entity-level) <= 0.02.

Operational notes: we'll version the model and keep an immutable run artifact for each bakeoff so we can reproduce the exact binary/config. For long-context prompts we'll validate KV-cache correctness by checking that references to earlier tokens remain stable across the streamed segments.

I'll attach the evaluation harness scripts in the Drive runbook and the CSV with specific run names.

—Karthik
